answer: Here is one mechanism that works: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because grove only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, prism is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any copper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
